bull_bear.body:
- Maiden dividend INR0.60/share (30% payout on FV) — commemorates Bajaj Group centenary + first profitable signal.
- Deleveraging: cash borrowings INR121 cr → INR31 cr; net D/EBITDA to 2.8x.
- Capex (INR170 cr) part debt-funded (INR120 cr term loan).
- SPV equity kept deliberately small — capital-light EPC stance, no asset ownership.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- Thin absolute margins (~4.4% EBITDA, ~1% PAT) — vulnerable to commodity/execution slippage.
- Commodity inflation (Al/steel/zinc/copper); steel & zinc unhedgeable; crude >$100, LPG shortage, FX depreciation.
- **Working capital:** debtors up INR590 cr (INR1,258→INR1,849 cr); NWC 124 days. Mgmt attributes to higher Q4 billing (+INR194 cr), one marquee customer holding ~INR225 cr in late March (since largely collected), and rising EPC retention (+~INR100 cr) — claims one-time, mostly recovered.
- US-Iran conflict slowing MENA ramp; manpower/skilled-labor shortage; new labor code raising costs.
- FY26 ordering "temporary moderation" industry-wide on capacity/bandwidth.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body:
- Inaugural call after >2 yrs listed — improving disclosure/IR posture. Chairman framed around Bajaj 100-yr legacy ("Kathni Karni Ek Si").
- Candid: openly flagged Q4 margin dip, commodity exposure, working-capital spike with specific numbers; directly addressed a skeptical retail question on SPV EPS dilution. Repeatedly stressed quality-over-scale and capital-light discipline. Credible, measured, "cautiously optimistic."
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The SPV is structured to be EPS-accretive, not dilutive: tiny equity, back-to-back EPC, exit at commissioning — a pipeline-sourcing device, not an asset play.
- "Quality-led growth" = deliberately capping top-line ambition (15%) while prioritizing margin/working-capital — a re-rating could come from margin, not revenue.
- In-sourcing capex is as much a supply-security play (tower capacity scarce as solar/wind compete) as a cost play.
- Fully 765 kV qualified (AIS+GIS) — HVDC is the only remaining capability gap, and they're actively hunting it.
- The INR225 cr marquee-customer withholding and trust MTM loss are non-structural — reported PAT understates underlying.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Committed capex of Rs.170 crore towards the Ranjangaon expansion is the only quantified spend commitment in the deck.
- "As of August 2026, Bajel Projects holds a 'CRISIL A+/ Stable & CRISIL A1' an upgrade in long term rating, reflecting its strong business and financial risk profiles."
- Management attributes profit growth to "prudent working capital management"; RAASTA 2030 sets a ">15% Return on Capital Employed" ambition.
- Capital is being deployed into international entities (50:50 MENA JV, 100% Abu Dhabi subsidiary) rather than any dividend or buyback - the deck makes no mention of dividend, buyback or debt-reduction policy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Tripartite SPV (Bajel + NIIF + AnantGrid):** announced 10-Mar-26. Bajel takes a SMALL equity stake (analyst cited ~26%); financing largely by NIIF/AnantGrid. Bajel gets back-to-back EPC contracts and is contractually EXITED at commissioning — explicitly NO long-term asset ownership / no O&M. Mgmt frames it as pipeline-quality enhancement and access to marquee LPs (CPP, ADIA-type sovereigns).
- **KSA JV (50:50 with Al Sharif):** long-term MENA platform.
- **5 employee-welfare trusts:** mark-to-market loss INR6.67 cr (FY)/INR1.57 cr (Q4) due to weak end-March equity prices; expected to reverse as markets recover — not a recurring operating item.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Part of the Bajaj Group, described as "India's 3rd largest group by market capitalization" with $167+Bn group market cap, 40+ group companies and 100 years in business; Bajel was demerged from Bajaj Electricals and separately listed on Indian stock exchanges on 19th Dec'23 as a "distinct, sector focused, listed entity".
- Claims 25+ years of impact in power infrastructure with 10,193+ ckm of transmission lines, 49+ AIS/GIS substations works, 1,158+ monopoles supplied, 1,100+ km of underground cabling and 80,582+ transformers installed (deck marks the transformer figure "*Revised").
- Combined EPC + manufacturing model with global EPC + product presence in 9+ countries; EPC executed in Kenya, Togo, Zambia and Egypt, product supplies to 9+ countries.
- Qualification depth is presented as the moat: experience across 132 kV, 220 kV, 400 kV and 765 kV lines in S/C, D/C and M/C configurations, qualified to bid for AIS and GIS substations up to <=765 kV, and "Actively pursuing 800 kV HVDC projects".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Demerger] "Successfully demerged from Bajaj Electricals Limited leading to formation of Bajel Projects Limited" in 2023; separately listed on 19th Dec'23.
- [Segment rename] "Power Distribution business has been renamed as New Energies".
- [JV / Subsidiary] Incorporated ASC Bajel JV (50:50 with Al-Sharif Group, MENA) and Bajel T&D Projects and Contracting LLC (100% subsidiary, Abu Dhabi, for the GCC region).
- [Regulation] An exceptional item in FY'26 is footnoted as "one time provision made towards new labor code".
- [Strategy phase] Deck states "We are successfully transitioning into the 'Prepare for Scale' phase" of the RAASTA 2030 six-year roadmap to FY'30.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- FY26 EBITDA margin 4.4% (+100 bps); Q4 3.7% (sequential dip vs ~4.8% prior qtr).
- Exposed to aluminum, zinc, steel, copper. Aluminum largely hedged through FY26 (some open exposure on new orders); steel/zinc effectively un-hedgeable.
- Steel rose post safeguard-duty imposition; depreciating INR added pressure.
- Margin levers: in-sourcing tower/monopole (lower COGS), Project NEEV digitization, disciplined bidding, customer price relief talks.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
**This quarter (Q4/FY26):**
- First-ever >INR1,000 cr quarter (Q4 rev INR1,008 cr, +26% YoY); FY26 rev INR2,792 cr (+7%).
- FY26 EBITDA margin +100 bps to 4.4%; but Q4 margin DIPPED to 3.7% (vs ~4.8% prior qtr) on commodity spike.
- Maiden dividend INR0.60/sh declared. Inaugural earnings call held.
- Order inflow +55% YoY (~INR3,100 cr); OB INR3,442 cr. MSETCL INR700 cr TBCB win.
- NIIF/AnantGrid tripartite SPV + Al Sharif KSA 50:50 JV signed.
- Ranjangaon INR170 cr expansion announced (45kt→110-120kt).
- Labor-code exceptional INR7.72 cr; trust MTM loss INR6.67 cr (FY).

**Next-quarter / FY27 watch items:**
- Verify FY27 revenue tracks the "15%+" guide and OB closes at INR4,000-5,000 cr.
- Galvanizing bath commissioning by August 2026 (phase 1); watch capex pace (bulk this year).
- Conversion of INR2,000 cr L1 and INR22,000 cr pipeline; further MENA orders despite US-Iran drag.
- Margin recovery from 3.7% — does hedging / in-sourcing / customer relief restore the trajectory?
- Working-capital normalization (collection of withheld receivables, debtor-day trend).
- Any HVDC order entry — the stated capability gap.
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log

outlook.body:
- **Revenue growth: "upwards of 15%"** for FY27 ("quite confident we should get there"); explicitly NOT chasing top line, but acknowledges scale needed for fixed-cost absorption.
- **Order book target: INR4,000–5,000 cr unexecuted by end-FY27.**
- Margin: aim to protect/improve via hedging, in-sourcing, Project NEEV; customers being approached for relief on extraordinary commodity moves.
- Tone: "cautiously optimistic" entering FY27 given US-Iran conflict / MENA slowdown.
outlook.title: Guidance (next year — FY27)

outlook.body:
- Unexecuted OB INR3,442 cr (31-Mar-26). FY26 inflow ~INR3,100 cr (+55% YoY).
- Key FY26 wins: INR700 cr TBCB from MSETCL (400/220 kV substation + line, Saswad); PGCIL Mandsaur project; PGCIL Vindhyachal pool project.
- Post-March: >INR1,000 cr secured in first ~40 days of FY27, including **first MENA order ~INR400 cr** (500 kV overhead line).
- L1 / advanced negotiation: >INR2,000 cr. Active pursuit pipeline: **INR22,000 cr.**
- FY26 execution: commissioned 17 projects, 1,168 ckm (~10% of India's total transmission-line addition in FY26).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **HVDC:** NOT yet in portfolio but "keen" to add; fully qualified up to 765 kV (both GIS & AIS) so credentials no longer a constraint — waiting for the right opportunity.
- **Monopoles:** dedicated new line (phase 3) — mgmt sees high future demand and claims design + manufacturing edge.
- International: GCC/MENA/Africa (Saudi Vision 2030, UAE, Oman, Egypt) — selective, well-priced 500 kV tenders.
- RAASTA 2030: six-year roadmap — high-voltage complex EPC, selective profitable international, margin via digitization (Project NEEV), adjacent infra.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Pure-play 765 kV transmission EPC carve-out from Bajaj Electricals, pivoting from scale-led to quality-led growth — record >INR1,000 cr quarter, 100 bps FY26 EBITDA-margin lift, strong order inflow (+55% YoY) and first MENA win, but absolute margins still thin (~4.4%) and exposed to commodity/working-capital swings.

open.item: Approved expansion of galvanisation capacity at Ranjangaon from 40,500 MT per annum to 1,10,000 MT per annum, to be executed in phases.
Transition from Phase 1 'Gear for Growth' to Phase 2 'Prepare for Scale' under the RAASTA 2030 strategic journey, focusing on building institutional systems for scale.
Increasingly prioritising high-margin, high-voltage projects over pure revenue growth to improve earnings predictability and cash-flow discipline.
Announced a landmark 50:50 Joint Venture with Al Sharif Contracting and Commercial Development Company in Saudi Arabia to pursue EPC contracts in High Voltage and Extra High Voltage infrastructure.
Signed a tripartite collaboration agreement with National Investment and Infrastructure Fund and AnantGrid Private Limited to participate in India's transmission growth through a developer-EPC model.
Strengthen operational excellence through Project Neev, including mechanised tower erection, digital PMO tools, GPS-based fleet tracking, e-cataloguing, and real-time project monitoring.

Management explicitly flags exposure to project execution timelines, Right-of-Way challenges, working capital cycles, commodity input volatility, site safety, environmental compliance, customer concentration, and international expansion as key risks.
Appointment of a Senior Vice President & Business Head – International to drive international business.
Appointment of Senior Vice President & Business Head for SCM & Manufacturing to oversee supply chain and manufacturing.
Risk Management Committee tasked to identify, assess, mitigate and monitor existing and potential risks including cyber security and financial risk.
Corporate Social Responsibility Committee to formulate, recommend, and oversee CSR policies and programs.
Seeking member approval to authorize the Board to borrow up to an aggregate limit of ₹5,000 crore.
Seeking member approval to create mortgage/charge on assets up to an aggregate limit of ₹5,000 Crores to secure borrowings.

drhp.business: Bajel Projects Limited provides engineering, procurement, construction, testing, and commissioning services across power transmission, new energies, monopoles, and emerging adjacencies like data centers and battery storage. The company serves utilities, transmission developers, and industrial clients in India and select international markets, leveraging its Ranjangaon manufacturing facility for backward integration. It operates as a distinct listed entity following its demerger from Bajaj Electricals Limited in 2023, drawing on the governance standards of the Bajaj Group.

drhp.expansion: During FY26, the Company incurred capital expenditure of ₹37.56 crore, primarily towards property, plant and equipment, capital work-in-progress, and other intangible assets. As of March 31, 2026, gross fixed assets stood at ₹195.43 crore. The Company continues to focus on judicious management of working capital and cash flows to support its business requirements. No specific new capacity expansion projects with commissioning timelines were disclosed.
